## Are older insect lineages more species rich in Hawaiʻi?

Using product-moment [correlation]{.alert}, we got a "significant" correlation


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Pearson's product-moment correlation

data:  hi_insect$clade_age and hi_insect$clade_richness
t = 2.4884, df = 15, p-value = 0.02507
alternative hypothesis: true correlation is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 0.08093661 0.81059406
sample estimates:
      cor 
0.5405529 
```


:::
:::


## Are older insect lineages more species rich in Hawaiʻi?

The significant correlation means that clade age and number of species have a [predictive]{.alert} relationship (I could predict one from the other).

How do we actually predict number of species from clade age?

## Learning Objectives

1. Use linear regression to predict $Y$ based on $X$
2. Test the null hypothesis of slope = 0
3. Display uncertainty in predictions from a linear regression
4. Use diagnostic plots to evaluate if data meet assumptions of regression

## Showing steps for calculating regression models

Make some fake tooth decay data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# this makes all "random" numbers the same every time
# we run this code
set.seed(12)

# random dates
deltaC14 <- runif(18, 0, 600)

# simulate date of birth from slope, intercept,
# and residual error
dateOfBirth <- 1992.27 - 0.05326 * deltaC14 +
    rnorm(18, sd = 10.99)
```
:::


## Showing steps for calculating regression models

Make some fake tooth decay data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# combine into data.frame
tooth.data <- data.frame(deltaC14 = deltaC14,
                         dateOfBirth = dateOfBirth)

# have a look
head(tooth.data)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   deltaC14 dateOfBirth
1  41.61655    1994.757
2 490.66512    1957.590
3 565.57304    1947.928
4 161.62913    1975.094
5 101.60887    1986.990
6  20.33737    1989.512
```


:::
:::


## Showing steps for calculating regression models

Plot it


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(tooth.data, aes(deltaC14, dateOfBirth)) +
    geom_point()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](11-regression-slides_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=5.5in}
:::
:::


## Showing steps for calculating regression models

Make a linear model


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tooth.model <- lm(dateOfBirth ~ deltaC14,
                  data = tooth.data)
```
:::


## Showing steps for calculating regression models

Get info on null hypothesis tests


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(tooth.model)
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Call:
lm(formula = dateOfBirth ~ deltaC14, data = tooth.data)

Residuals:

deltaC14      -0.06529    0.01300  -5.024 0.000125 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Multiple R-squared:  0.612,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.5878

```


:::
:::

  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current

  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
